_why: Every published fact in the film is bounded by the fetched excerpts below. The validator deliberately rejected present-tense operation and an open application window because the sources do not establish either one.
story: A National Science Foundation cooperative agreement starts today to build an open-access autonomous alloy-discovery laboratory at Texas A&M, with machines assigned repetitive experimental work and researchers retaining judgment.

claims.statement: The cooperative agreement starts on September 1st, 2026.
claims.excerpt_of: National Science Foundation award record field
claims.source_type: primary official National Science Foundation award record

claims.statement: ARM-MIP is funded as an open-access national user facility that joins robotics, artificial intelligence, simulation and automated experimentation into one autonomous alloy laboratory.
claims.value_text: open-access national user facility and autonomous laboratory
claims.quote: The Autonomous Robotic Metallurgist Materials Innovation Platform (ARM-MIP) at Texas A&M University is an open-access national user facility that designs, makes, tests, and learns from new alloys, closing the discovery loop by integrating robotics, artificial intelligence, physics-based simulation, and automated experimentation into a single autonomous laboratory.
claims.source_type: primary official National Science Foundation award abstract

claims.statement: Outside researchers from universities, national laboratories and industry are intended to run discovery campaigns at the facility.
claims.value_text: outside researchers run their own discovery campaigns
claims.quote: scientists and engineers from universities, national laboratories, and industry come to ARM-MIP as hands-on users, running their own discovery campaigns and carrying autonomous-laboratory techniques back to their home institutions
claims.source_type: primary official National Science Foundation award abstract

claims.statement: The award divides repetitive work from research judgment.
claims.value_text: automation performs routine experimental work while researchers retain judgment
claims.quote: Automation handles sample fabrication, characterization, and routine computation, while researchers focus on hypothesis generation, interpretation, and the metallurgical decisions that drive discovery.
claims.source_type: primary official National Science Foundation award abstract

claims.statement: The planned loop melts, shapes, heat-treats and tests alloys, then uses the result to choose the next experiment.
claims.value_text: melt, shape, heat-treat, test, analyze, choose the next experiment
claims.quote: ARM-MIP’s robotic systems will melt, shape, heat-treat and test alloys around the clock. AI will analyze each result and choose what to make next — the way an experienced metallurgist would, but far faster and without delay. Simulations predict what is likely to happen before any metal is poured, so the robots spend their time on experiments worth running. The loop runs continuously and sharpens with every batch.

claims.statement: The planned facility is at the Texas A&M System RELLIS campus in Bryan.
claims.quote: ARM-MIP will be sited at The Texas A&M University System RELLIS Campus in Bryan

claims.statement: The national platform is planned for use in person and remotely.
claims.value_text: researchers may ship samples or send a scientific question
claims.quote: Researchers can also use the facility remotely, shipping samples or sending a scientific question and letting the platform help plan and execute the work.

claims.statement: Access will be selected through competitive review.
claims.quote: Each platform will host dozens of visiting scientists each year to conduct experiments, which are selected through a competitive review process.
claims.source_type: primary official National Science Foundation announcement

claims.statement: The funded platform is described prospectively and still has to be established.
claims.value_text: will establish and will be based
claims.quote: A six-year, $24.9 million grant from the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) will establish the Autonomous Robotic Metallurgist Materials Innovation Platform (ARM-MIP) at Texas A&M University

rejected.claim: The autonomous alloy laboratory is operating today.
rejected.reason: Rejected. The sources use future tense and say the award will establish the facility. The award starts today, not the robots.

rejected.claim: Researchers can apply for facility time today.
rejected.reason: Rejected. The sources say access will use competitive review but identify no open user call, application page or deadline.

rejected.claim: The new facility has already accelerated alloy discovery by a stated factor.
rejected.reason: Rejected. The acceleration figure belongs to the earlier BIRDSHOT proof-of-concept program, not to the not-yet-built ARM-MIP facility.

rejected.claim: The planned loop will produce experiments in weeks instead of years.
rejected.reason: Rejected from narration. It is a forward-looking institutional quotation and is not needed to explain the verified mechanism.
